Playbook.name: Windows — File and Directory Permissions Modification - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Defense Evasion / File and Directory Permissions Modification

Technique.name: Windows File and Directory Permissions Modification

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: icacls/cacls/takeown modified file/directory permissions with broad grants (:F, /grant, /setowner, /reset). Triage question: is an attacker weakening permissions to access/modify protected files, or a legitimate admin/installer permission change?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Attackers loosen ACLs to read protected data, replace binaries, or establish persistence; takeown+icacls is common before tampering with a protected file.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the permission change is attacker ACL weakening or a legitimate admin/installer action.

Step.name: What was re-permissioned and how broadly
Step.Purpose: The target path and grant reveal whether a sensitive/system location was opened up.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.name RLIKE "(?i)(icacls|cacls|takeown)(.exe)?" AND process.command_line IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, process.name, process.parent.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: Everyone:F or a grant on a system/Windows path, or takeown of a protected binary, is suspicious. An installer setting ACLs on its own Program Files dir is benign. The target path and the grantee are decisive.

Step.name: Process origin and account on the host
Step.Purpose: The parent process and account reveal whether this was interactive attacker activity or an automated/service context.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS runs = COUNT(*), parents = VALUES(process.parent.name), users = VALUES(user.name) BY process.name | SORT runs DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: A suspicious process spawned by an office app/browser/script interpreter, run by a normal user, is more concerning than one under a known admin/automation parent.

Node.Condition: Broad grants (Everyone:F) or takeown on system/sensitive paths by a non-admin or suspicious parent.
Node.Result: True Positive (ACL Weakening - investigate, likely pre-tamper)

Node.Condition: An installer/admin setting ACLs on its own application directory under a change.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-PERMS-DETAIL, INV-02-PROC-TREE to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the software/change; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Attacker weakening ACLs to access/modify protected files.

SOCAction.Item: Restore correct ACLs; inspect what the loosened path protected; open IR if tampering followed.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A deployment tool over-permissioning by design.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
